title: Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering

record.title: Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering
record.abstract: Patch-based ECG monitors are increasingly deployed for continuous ambulatory cardiac surveillance, yet their clinical utility is severely limited by high false-positive rates for atrial fibrillation (AF) alarms, largely attributable to motion artifacts. This paper presents a motion-aware filtering framework that fuses single-lead ECG signals with three-axis accelerometer data recorded simultaneously by the same wearable patch. The proposed method employs an adaptive notch filter whose coefficients are dynamically updated according to a motion-intensity index derived from accelerometer magnitude. A subsequent AF detector based on RR-interval irregularity metrics is applied to the cleaned signal. The system was evaluated on a dataset of 312 twenty-four-hour recordings collected from 89 volunteers performing standardized daily activities including walking, stair climbing, and cycling. Compared with a baseline detector operating on raw ECG, the proposed approach reduced false AF alarms by 61% while maintaining sensitivity above 94% on confirmed AF episodes verified by a board-certified cardiologist. Processing latency was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, confirming real-time feasibility. The results demonstrate that tightly coupled motion-aware signal conditioning is essential for trustworthy AF screening in free-living conditions.
